### Biological categories and taxonomic uncertainty

The primary analysis includes identified weed codes and unidentified groups so that all measured weed dry mass contributes to composition. The identified-code sensitivity analysis quantifies how the treatment results depend on those unresolved groups. Volunteer clover and sown cover crops are summarized separately.

```{r sampling-summary}
show_table(data.frame(
  Retained_records = sum(category_summary$Records),
  Samples = sum(plot_means$N_quadrats[plot_means$Analysis == "Total weeds"])
))
```

```{r category-mass}
show_table(select(category_summary, Broad_category, Records, Biomass_g,
                  Percent_of_recorded_mass))
```

## Quadrat-level indices and independent plot means

| Parameter | Why it was chosen for these harvest samples | Reference |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Dry biomass share, \(p_i=b_i/\sum b_i\) | A label's dry mass divided by the quadrat's included weed dry mass measures its contribution to standing biomass. The field measurements support weighting by dry mass. | Nguyen & Liebman (2022) |
| Recorded richness, \(S\) | Counts positive-mass weed labels once per quadrat, giving a low-biomass label the same weight as a dominant one. This measures how many recorded categories persist under each mowing schedule. | Hill (1973), Nguyen & Liebman (2022) |
| Inverse Simpson diversity, \(D_2=1/\sum p_i^2\) | Squaring biomass shares emphasizes dominant weeds. The reciprocal gives the effective number of equally abundant categories that would produce the observed concentration. | Hill (1973) |
| Simpson evenness, \(E=D_2/S\) | Expresses effective diversity relative to the observed number of categories. It measures how evenly the mass is distributed and equals one when all positive-mass categories have equal shares. | Tuomisto (2012) |

All 64 sampled quadrats had positive weed dry mass under both inclusion rules. Each index was calculated within each quadrat and then averaged within its plot and sampling stratum. Each experimental plot therefore contributes one observation per stratum (Hurlbert, 1984).

```{r plot-mean-indices}
show_table(filter(plot_means, Analysis == "Total weeds"))
```

## Biomass by broad category

A category absent from a sampled quadrat contributes zero recorded mass. Treatment summaries average quadrats within each plot, then give the four blocks equal weight. Broccoli rows and living-mulch strips are summarized separately.

```{r category-biomass-results}
show_table(select(
  category_treatments, Stratum, Treatment, Broad_category, N_plots,
  Mean_quadrat_biomass_g, Mean_biomass_g_m2, SE_biomass_g_m2
))
```

## Weed community composition at harvest

Each panel shows the five identified weeds with the highest mean dry biomass in its sampling stratum. Rankings give equal weight to each treatment mean: T2–T4 in broccoli rows and T1–T4 in the interrow comparison. Others pools the remaining identified species and all unidentified weed groups. The primary diversity indices use the full weed community.

```{r composition-display-groups}
sp_top <- sp_means |>
  filter(!startsWith(Species, "UNKNOWN")) |>
  group_by(Stratum, Species) |>
  summarise(rank_biomass = mean(Mean_biomass_g_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(rank_biomass > 0) |>
  arrange(Stratum, desc(rank_biomass), Species) |>
  group_by(Stratum) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  ungroup()

sp_display <- sp_means |>
  left_join(
    transmute(sp_top, Stratum, Species, Display_group = Species),
    by = c("Stratum", "Species")
  ) |>
  mutate(Display_group = coalesce(Display_group, "Others")) |>
  group_by(Treatment, Stratum, Display_group) |>
  summarise(Mean_biomass_g_m2 = sum(Mean_biomass_g_m2), .groups = "drop")

sp_totals <- sp_means |>
  group_by(Treatment, Stratum) |>
  summarise(Mean_biomass_g_m2 = sum(Mean_biomass_g_m2), .groups = "drop")

display_check <- sp_display |>
  group_by(Treatment, Stratum) |>
  summarise(groups = n(), displayed = sum(Mean_biomass_g_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(sp_totals, by = c("Treatment", "Stratum"))

stopifnot(
  all(display_check$groups == 6L),
  all(abs(display_check$displayed - display_check$Mean_biomass_g_m2) < 1e-8)
)
write_csv(sp_display, "Species_composition_display_groups.csv")
write_csv(sp_totals, "Species_composition_total_weeds.csv")
```

```{r composition-plot-function}
make_species_plot <- function(stratum, subtitle) {
  local_groups <- c(sp_top$Species[sp_top$Stratum == stratum], "Others")
  d <- filter(sp_display, Stratum == stratum) |>
    mutate(Display_group = factor(Display_group, levels = local_groups))

  treatment_order <- paste0("T", 1:4)
  axis_labels <- setNames(paste0(treatment_order, "\nNot sampled"), treatment_order)
  totals <- filter(total_means, Stratum == stratum)
  trt <- as.character(totals$Treatment)
  axis_labels[trt] <- sprintf("%s\n%.1f \u00b1 %.1f", trt, totals$emmean, totals$SE)

  ggplot(d, aes(Treatment, Mean_biomass_g_m2, fill = Display_group)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.86), width = 0.80) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = sp_colors, breaks = local_groups, labels = unname(sp_labels[local_groups])) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = treatment_order, labels = axis_labels) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = composition_breaks, limits = range(composition_breaks),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03))
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
    labs(
      title = "Weed community composition at broccoli harvest", subtitle = subtitle,
      x = "Treatment (total weed biomass marginal mean \u00b1 SE)",
      y = expression(Mean~weed~dry~biomass~(g~m^{-2})), fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey91", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position = "top",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    )
}
```

## Mowing effects on weed diversity

The primary comparison uses the three planted mowing treatments. T2 was mown one week before transplanting and at weeks 3 and 6 afterward. T3 was mown one week before and at week 6 afterward. T4 was mown one week before transplanting. The secondary interrow comparison includes the unplanted weedy control (T1).

### Statistical choices and their rationale

| Choice | Rationale in this experiment | Reference |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Response and unit | The response is the mean quadrat index of a plot. Each of the four blocks contributes one plot per treatment. This gives each randomized plot equal weight, including T1 plots with four quadrats. | Hurlbert (1984) |
| Sampling stratum | Intrarow and interrow samples differ in quadrat area and cutting height. Separate models compare treatments measured with the same protocol. | 2026 field sampling design |
| Model | Fit each index on its original scale as `index ~ Block + Treatment`. The fixed block term accounts for differences among the four field blocks. One plot per block–treatment cell supports an additive model. Collection date is determined by block. | NIST, *Randomized block designs* |
| Primary test statistic | The treatment F statistic compares between-treatment variation with residual variation after accounting for block. It tests for differences in any direction. | NIST, *Randomized block designs* |
| Randomization and exact p value | Conditional on the T1 position, permute the three planted treatment labels only within their own block. Enumerate all \((3!)^4=1,296\) assignments. The exact p value is the fraction with F at least as large as observed under the sharp null of no plot-level treatment effect. | Anderson & ter Braak (2003) |
| Multiple tests | Three indices in two strata give six primary tests. Report raw and Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjusted p values for this family. The identified-code sensitivity analysis and the three secondary tests each form a separate family. | Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) |
| Means and contrasts | Equal block weights estimate mean treatment responses across the four blocks. Pointwise 95% intervals describe uncertainty in each mean. Tukey adjustment covers all pairwise contrasts within one index and stratum. | Lenth (2016), Tukey (1949) |
| Diagnostics | Residual-versus-fitted plots assess spread. Normal Q–Q plots and Shapiro–Wilk W assess residual shape. Cook's distance flags influential plots for inspection. | Shapiro & Wilk (1965), Cook (1977) |

```{r enumerate-assignments}
orders <- rbind(
  c(1, 2, 3), c(1, 3, 2), c(2, 1, 3),
  c(2, 3, 1), c(3, 1, 2), c(3, 2, 1)
)
assignments <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(seq_len(nrow(orders))), 4)))
stopifnot(nrow(assignments) == 1296L)
```

```{r exact-block-test}
exact_rcbd <- function(y) {
  stopifnot(identical(dim(y), c(4L, 3L)), all(is.finite(y)))

  centered <- sweep(y, 1, rowMeans(y))
  total_ss <- sum(centered^2)
  if (total_ss == 0) {
    stop("No within-block variation for the randomization test.")
  }

  # Treatment SS and F have the same ordering when block totals are fixed.
  observed <- sum(colSums(centered)^2) / nrow(y)
  sums <- matrix(0, nrow(assignments), ncol(y))

  for (b in seq_len(nrow(y))) {
    permuted <- matrix(centered[b, ][orders], nrow = nrow(orders))
    sums <- sums + permuted[assignments[, b], , drop = FALSE]
  }

  permuted_ss <- rowSums(sums^2) / nrow(y)
  tolerance <- 64 * .Machine$double.eps * total_ss
  mean(permuted_ss >= observed - tolerance)
}
```

```{r model-inputs}
select_plots <- function(analysis, stratum, treatments) {
  d <- plot_means[
    plot_means$Analysis == analysis &
      plot_means$Stratum == stratum &
      plot_means$Treatment %in% treatments,
  ]

  d$Treatment <- factor(d$Treatment, levels = treatments)
  d$Block <- factor(d$Block, levels = paste0("B", 1:4))

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(d$Block),
    all(table(d$Block, d$Treatment) == 1L)
  )

  d[order(d$Block, d$Treatment), ]
}
```

```{r fit-one-index}
fit_index <- function(d, metric, use_exact) {
  if (any(!is.finite(d[[metric]]))) {
    stop(
      "A plot has an undefined ", metric, " in ", d$Stratum[1],
      " (", d$Analysis[1], "). Inspect Plot_mean_indices.csv."
    )
  }

  fit <- lm(
    reformulate(c("Block", "Treatment"), metric),
    data = d, na.action = na.fail
  )
  a <- anova(fit)
  y <- matrix(d[[metric]], nrow = nlevels(d$Block), byrow = TRUE)
  id <- data.frame(Analysis = d$Analysis[1], Stratum = d$Stratum[1], Metric = metric)

  tests <- cbind(
    id,
    N_plots = nrow(d),
    F = a["Treatment", "F value"],
    df1 = a["Treatment", "Df"],
    df2 = df.residual(fit),
    Parametric_p = a["Treatment", "Pr(>F)"],
    Exact_p = if (use_exact) exact_rcbd(y) else NA_real_,
    Permutations = if (use_exact) nrow(assignments) else NA_integer_
  )

  em <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ Treatment, weights = "equal")
  means <- as.data.frame(confint(em, level = 0.95, adjust = "none"))
  pairs_table <- as.data.frame(summary(
    pairs(em), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95, adjust = "tukey"
  ))

  sh <- shapiro.test(residuals(fit))
  diagnostics <- cbind(
    id,
    Residual_SD = sigma(fit),
    Shapiro_W = unname(sh$statistic),
    Shapiro_p = sh$p.value,
    Max_Cooks_distance = max(cooks.distance(fit))
  )

  list(
    tests = tests,
    emmeans = cbind(means, id[rep(1L, nrow(means)), , drop = FALSE]),
    pairs = cbind(pairs_table, id[rep(1L, nrow(pairs_table)), , drop = FALSE]),
    diagnostics = diagnostics,
    model = fit
  )
}
```

```{r run-model-family}
run_family <- function(analysis, strata, treatments, use_exact) {
  fits <- list()

  for (s in strata) {
    d <- select_plots(analysis, s, treatments)
    for (m in metrics) {
      fits[[paste(s, m, sep = " / ")]] <- fit_index(d, m, use_exact)
    }
  }

  collect <- function(field) {
    x <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, "[[", field))
    rownames(x) <- NULL
    x
  }

  tests <- collect("tests")
  tests$Exact_p_BH <- if (use_exact) p.adjust(tests$Exact_p, "BH") else NA_real_
  tests$Parametric_p_BH <- p.adjust(tests$Parametric_p, "BH")

  list(
    tests = tests,
    emmeans = collect("emmeans"),
    pairs = collect("pairs"),
    diagnostics = collect("diagnostics"),
    models = lapply(fits, "[[", "model")
  )
}
```

```{r primary-models}
strata <- c("Cover_crop", "Broccoli")
planted <- c("T2", "T3", "T4")

primary <- run_family("Total weeds", strata, planted, TRUE)
show_table(primary$tests)
```

```{r primary-means-and-contrasts}
show_table(primary$emmeans)
show_table(primary$pairs)
```

### Sensitivity to unidentified weeds

The identified-code analysis repeats the six tests after removing unidentified weed groups. The quadrat table records the fraction of weed dry mass removed from each sample.

```{r sensitivity-models}
sensitivity <- run_family("Identified weed codes", strata, planted, TRUE)
show_table(sensitivity$tests)
```

### Secondary comparison with the weedy control

This exploratory comparison uses the 0.16 m² quadrats cut at 8 cm. Contrasts with T1 reflect planting and mowing together. T1 contributes four quadrats per plot and T2–T4 contribute two, so the precision of a plot mean can differ among treatments. This analysis reports the parametric treatment test.

```{r secondary-models}
secondary <- run_family("Total weeds", "Cover_crop", paste0("T", 1:4), FALSE)
show_table(secondary$tests)
show_table(secondary$emmeans)
show_table(secondary$pairs)
```

```{r export-model-tables, include=FALSE}
export_family <- function(x, prefix) {
  write_csv(x$tests, paste0(prefix, "_tests.csv"))
  write_csv(x$emmeans, paste0(prefix, "_emmeans.csv"))
  write_csv(x$pairs, paste0(prefix, "_Tukey_pairs.csv"))
}

export_family(primary, "Primary_T2_T4")
export_family(sensitivity, "Sensitivity_identified_codes_T2_T4")
export_family(secondary, "Secondary_T1_T4_Cover_crop")
write_csv(primary$diagnostics, "Primary_model_diagnostics.csv")
```

## Model diagnostics

```{r diagnostic-table}
show_table(primary$diagnostics)
```

```{r diagnostic-figures, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
plot_diagnostics <- function(fit, title) {
  old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
  on.exit(par(old))

  plot(
    fitted(fit), residuals(fit),
    xlab = "Fitted value", ylab = "Residual",
    main = title, pch = 19, cex.main = 0.85
  )
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

  qqnorm(residuals(fit), main = "Residual normal Q–Q", pch = 19)
  qqline(residuals(fit))
}

for (name in names(primary$models)) {
  plot_diagnostics(primary$models[[name]], name)
}
```

Inference concerns the 2026 harvest and the randomized plots. The adjacent plastic-mulched beds serve as a production benchmark outside the diversity analysis.

## References

- Nguyen, H. T. X., & Liebman, M. (2022). Weed community composition in simple and more diverse cropping systems. *Frontiers in Agronomy*. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fagro.2022.848548>
- Hill, M. O. (1973). Diversity and evenness: A unifying notation and its consequences. *Ecology*. <https://doi.org/10.2307/1934352>
- Tuomisto, H. (2012). An updated consumer's guide to evenness and related indices. *Oikos*. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1600-0706.2011.19897.x>
- Hurlbert, S. H. (1984). Pseudoreplication and the design of ecological field experiments. *Ecological Monographs*. <https://doi.org/10.2307/1942661>
- NIST/SEMATECH. *e-Handbook of Statistical Methods*, §5.3.3.2, Randomized block designs. <https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section3/pri332.htm>
- Anderson, M. J., & ter Braak, C. J. F. (2003). Permutation tests for multi-factorial analysis of variance. *Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation*. <https://doi.org/10.1080/00949650215733>
- Benjamini, Y., & Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: A practical and powerful approach to multiple testing. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B*. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x>
